technical_validation.duplicate_guard_evidence: r4 checkpoint/rebuild paths reject duplicate ownership; current registry read found one owner per frozen target.
technical_validation.qualification: Mutable global registry was read only for ownership and not hash-locked.

items.evidence: Paragraph 192 describes anticipated reputational consequences and distress within the costs discussion.
items.scope_review: It supplies no independent damages test or entitlement and expressly says Web dissemination had not yet occurred.

items.evidence: Paragraph 46 says that because applicant counsel did not object at the hearing, the Court would consider every respondent argument while reserving possible remedy-and-cost consequences.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is a case-specific procedural choice, not a universal waiver rule or validation of the respondent's arguments.

items.evidence: The Sopinka majority quotation separately supports investigator-as-Commission-extension/delegation and CHRC screening on reasonable evidentiary basis rather than merits adjudication, with procedural fairness retained.
items.scope_review: Qualification: both AUs are cited-court propositions in the CHRA filtering context. The absence of formal natural-justice rules does not eliminate procedural fairness and cannot be transferred to the PSEA section 69 scheme. The two primary evidence spans are disjoint.

items.evidence: Paragraph 139 recounts interview chronology, representation and questioning under oath.
items.scope_review: The applicant's earlier exclusion is a case fact; this target creates neither a standalone oath entitlement nor a jurisdiction holding.

items.evidence: Paragraph 85 separately states PSDPA section 9 discipline for wrongdoing, including termination, and FAA section 12 deputy-head authority to discipline and terminate staff under their authority.
items.scope_review: Qualification: PSDPA discipline is appropriate-action language conditioned on wrongdoing, not automatic dismissal; FAA authority is limited to public servants under the deputy head. Neither AU grants PSEA Commission jurisdiction. The primary spans are adjacent but non-overlapping.

items.evidence: Paragraph 195 holds that ensuring institutional confidence cannot justify the unfair means used by this investigator in this case.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is case-specific and not a categorical prohibition on e-mail interception. Paragraph 196 expressly declines to declare the applicant innocent.

items.evidence: Paragraph 23 states that where no respondent can be named under Rule 303(1), Rule 303(2) requires naming the Attorney General of Canada.
items.scope_review: Qualification: Rule 303(3), described immediately afterward, permits court-ordered substitution on the Attorney General's motion when its conditions are met. The AU is not a never-name-the-tribunal rule.

items.evidence: Paragraph 37 recounts respondent advocacy from another case about lateness, guilt and corrective measures.
items.scope_review: The current court criticizes the advocacy posture and does not adopt the quoted propositions.

items.evidence: Paragraph 19 describes another appointment process, references, non-appointment and an agency fraud finding.
items.scope_review: It is not an adjudication of this applicant's guilt or an adopted legal definition of fraud.

items.evidence: Paragraph 109 contrasts the greater legitimate expectations of a person suspected of fraud in a PSEA section 69 investigation with a discrimination case.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the comparative proposition does not itself specify a mandatory hearing format or erase the distinct CHRC framework discussed afterward.

boundaries.note: Only frozen twelfth10 decisions are accepted; mutable overall progress is outside scope.
